title: Fleet runway scenarios, order cadence lattice
content:
Purpose:
Quick, scenario-driven planning sheet to translate burn-rate signals into realistic order cadence windows and region-aware SKU mixes. This is intentionally lightweight (spreadsheet-style) for ops/infra syncs — use as the single-pane input for procurement requests and SRE capacity forecasts.

High-level assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline 6w burn measured as tokens-equivalent converted to vGPU-hours from telemetry-pipeline (see INFRA-Runway-2025).
- Target overall utilization: 72% steady-state (with 85% burst window).
- Safety buffer: 18% fleet-level (regional buffers vary, see table).
- Preferred SKU order sizes: multiples of rack-equivalent (8 A100-80GB or 4 H100-80GB per rack) to reduce provisioning friction.
- Lead time ranges (procurement + shipping + customs) are highly SKU-specific and region-dependent; treat low end as optimistic plan, high end as contingency.

Key outcome required from this doc: discrete buy windows (W1..W6), SKU mix per window, per-region allocation %, trigger conditions (alerts), and a short decision tree for accelerated lanes (spot leasing / 3rd-party bursts).

Summary table (canonical view):
Columns: Window | ETA (min-max wks) | SKU mix (pct) | Units ordered (rack equiv) | Region split (NA|EU|APAC) | Trigger metric
W1 | 6-10 wks | H100-heavy (60% H100, 30% A100, 10% L40) | 12 racks | 60|30|10 | burn > baseline + 12% for 2w
W2 | 10-16 wks | Balanced (40% H100, 50% A100, 10% L40) | 20 racks | 55|30|15 | rolling avg utilization > 75% for 3w
W3 | 16-26 wks | A100-heavy (70% A100, 20% H100, 10% misc) | 24 racks | 50|35|15 | capacity shortfall forecasted > 10% peak 12w
W4 | 26-40 wks | Cost-saving tranche (60% A100 40% L40S) | 30 racks | 50|30|20 | procurement pricing window opens (vendor alert)
W5 | 40-60 wks | Strategic backfill (mix for long lead replacements) | 16 racks | 45|35|20 | long-term contract re-up negotiation (>= Q3)
W6 | 8-24 wks | Emergency lease lane (third-party burst) | on-demand | dynamic | dynamic | immediate surge > 30% baseline or sustained cloud overage > $200k/mo

Regional lead time insight (notes):
- NA: shortest baseline transit for most SKUs but customs/local warehouse backlog can add 2-4w.
- EU: H100 lead times commonly +6-12w compared to A100 due to channel constraints; plan earlier for H100-heavy windows.
- APAC: strong variability, plan +8w on average for any new SKU, prefer leasing partnerships for short-term need.

SKU-specific heuristics:
- H100-80GB: highest throughput for LLMs; best for low-latency, high-throughput hosted endpoints. Cost per effective token lowest when utilized >65%. Avoid small single-rack buys unless committed to 12+ months.
- A100-80GB: versatile; strong price/perf for mixed workloads and cheaper procurement cadence. Good for Dedicated pools where cost predictability matters.
- L40S / L40: emerging cost-efficient SKU for embedding/cheap batch workloads. Useful as fallback for non-critical background jobs and cache warmers.

Inventory ledger snapshot (as of 2026-02-18):
- On-hand (active): H100: 96 units (equiv 24 racks), A100: 160 units (equiv 20 racks), L40: 72 units (equiv 9 racks)
- Committed (incoming): 48 H100 (in-trailer NA, ETA 9 wks), 120 A100 (ETA 18 wks EU staging), 0 L40 (no committed)
- Allocated to Dedicated customers: ~42% of active fleet; Host API steady state uses 38%; reserve/unassigned 20%

Short scenarios (decision lattice) — rapid reference:
1) Mild growth (+10% burn over 8w): Trigger W1 order, prefer H100 partial + A100 top-up. Request procurement to target NA rack shipments to minimize ETA.
2) Seasonal surge (+30% over 4w): Engage W6 (leasing) and accelerate W2 orders; pre-empty low-priority background jobs onto L40s; temporarily raise batching windows for embeddings to curb token burn.
3) Vendor slip (H100 ETA pushes +6w): Pull-forward A100 tranche from W3 and reassign burst lanes to lease partners; optionally re-quantize non-latency-critical models to 4-bit to free H100 demand.
4) Downturn (sustained -15% usage): Defer prepaid orders in W4/W5; negotiate flexible delivery windows with vendors; explore subleasing racks for short windows.

Operational runbook snippets (for SRE / procurement):
- Alert mapping: utilization_alert_75pct -> review capacity dashboard -> if forecasted shortfall >= 8% for 4w -> raise procurement request tag JIRA-3421 and assign to procurement lead.
- Procurement SLA expectations: vendor confirmation 2w, manufacturing lead times per vendor (see vendor matrix), shipping + customs variable.
- Short-term leases: pre-approved vendors: VendorX (NA), LeaseAP (APAC), QuickBurstEU (EU). Contracts: Master Lease template v2 attached in Confluence.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: SKU deprecation / EOL signals from vendor -> Mitigate: prioritize flexible mix purchases, prefer vendors with predictable revision timelines and spare-parts support.
- Risk: Region-specific customs delay -> Mitigate: keep 2-rack warm buffer per region, pre-clear customs documentation in procurement checklist.
- Risk: Price volatility on H100 -> Mitigate: ladder buys across windows to smooth spot spikes; use committed tranches to lock-in when beneficial.

Open questions / items to resolve (notes to self):
- Confirm whether Dedicated enterprise customers are ok with A100-only replacement for lower-risk features (ticket: JIRA-3498).
- Get APAC vendor contact for expedited shipping lanes and add to approved vendor list.
- Reconcile procurement currency risk assumptions with Finance (FX hedge or not?) before W4 commits.

Decision log (short):
- 2026-01-09 — Agreed on 18% safety buffer fleet-target (meeting notes INFRA-Runway-2025). Owner: Miguel.
- 2026-02-05 — Approve W1 procurement request draft (JIRA-3421). Owner: Aisha.

Action items (this doc owner):
- [ ] Finalize NA shipment routing with Ops by 2026-02-25.
- [ ] Lock preliminary vendor quotes for W2 by 2026-03-10.
- [ ] Add L40S push-plan for background workloads and update routing rules.

Quick calc examples (tools-free):
- If baseline rack-hour burn = 1200 rack-hours/week and H100 effective throughput demands increase by 15% -> equivalent of ~3 additional racks of H100 needed to keep latency SLOs.
- Safety buffer computation: Required capacity = baseline/(1 - safety_buffer). Example: baseline 100 racks / (1 - 0.18) = 121 racks -> order delta = 21 racks.

References & links:
- INFRA-Runway-2025 (Confluence) for telemetry mappings
- JIRA-3421 procurement request ticket
- GitHub ops-procure PR #78 for automated vendor quote ingestion

Notes (informal):
- This sheet is intentionally tactical; for long-term strategy, fold into the FY26 procurement plan doc.
- Keep communications short when raising alerts — procurement gets many asks; include ETA ranges and preferred rack breakouts.
